title: Buying piano records in Dallas and his parents' tastes
summary: A music-store clerk saved piano solos for him all year, including Cow Cow Davenport, Jelly Roll Morton and Clarence Williams. The family bought them on fall trips to Dallas after the cotton sale, and his parents simply liked what he liked.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, there was a Miss Hazel Booth at Whittle's Music Company who would put aside all through the year all piano solos that would come in. We had, I remember, things by Kalkia Davenport and old Jelly Roll, lots of Jelly Roll Martin pieces and Clarence Williams, early Wildflower Rag and Argan Grindr Blues and Kansas City Stomp by Jelly, Seattle Hunch. And in the fall, when Daddy would sell cotton and all, we had money, we'd go to Dallas quite frequently. And then we'd go by there, buy all those records that she had put aside all through the year waiting for me to come up.
It was mainly piano music that they liked.
Oh yeah. I was always, you know, it was all.
Were they buying them for you or for them?
Oh no, these were mine. These were for you? This was a kid always at home, you know, they were, and they would have just, before I could talk, even they'd bring home player roles and give it to me.
How did their own musical tastes run?

Oh, I don't think they really had much of, they weren't primarily interested in that. They were familiar, they liked what I liked, and they got what was coming out to the whole market, all kinds of pieces.
